cohort: targeted source-first risk review; not random; no completeness or task-eligibility claim

findings.reading: Anonymous Mishnah requires seven-day separation and substitute priest lest disqualification occur. R Judah adds substitute wife lest she die, deriving house=wife; unnamed respondents object that this has no end. Do not treat objection as Judah's maintained claim.

Parah priest separated seven days northeast in stone chamber. Vessels prevent impurity and counteract contempt generated by deliberate impurification/immersion, which opposes Sadducee sunset requirement. Northeast combines chatat north and facing sanctuary east.
Explicit question מאי בירה. Rabbah bar bar Hanah reports R Yohanan: a named place on Temple Mount. Resh Lakish: entire Temple called bira; cited verse supports latter, not Yohanan.

Menyomi b Hilqiyah -> Mahsiah b Idi -> Yohanan reports לעשות parah / לכפר YK. Later 3b:11 limits this to Yohanan transmitting his teacher R Ishmael. Anonymous objection proposes entire verse YK; answer derives parah via צוה צוה. פרה לאו בת כפרה is literal negation.

Objections propose YK צוה then sacrifices צותו. Answers distinguish before versus after action, same word versus other form. School of R Ishmael equates שב ובא as challenge to lexical exclusion; resolution permits unlike wording only where no matching wording available. Conditions cannot be dropped.

Proposals: sacrifices, festivals, one festival; sequential responses fixed time, once yearly, seven-day separation for one day. Initial challenge not knowing priest is countered by separating full watch/house, so do not encode it as final impossibility. Single festival options Pesach first in scripture versus Sukkot many mitzvot are hypothetical proposals.

Proposed Shemini Atzeret rejected for prior sanctity; a fortiori objection answered by Rav Mesharshiya הזה=כזה. Rav Ashi separately rejects secondary festival separation where main festival lacks it. Even view Shemini independent is confined to PZR QShB; for compensatory offerings it belongs to first festival. Scope crosses folio and segment.

Shavuot proposal answered by R Abba one bull/one ram analogy; objection: Eliezer b Shimon counts two YK rams versus Rabbi one identical ram across texts. Resolution distinguishes YK one obligation of day plus one musaf, versus Shavuot both day obligation. Do not erase disagreement or conditional answer.

R Abbahu own bull/ram analogy excludes Shavuot and RH communal animals. Objection raises take/make for yourself views; R Yoshiyah distinguishes own vs communal wording, R Yonatan both communal with preference wording. Abba Hanan reports R Eleazar reconciling ark texts by whether Israel does God's will; exact mapping of each verse not explicit locally. Disagreement only ordinary takings/makings; explicit YK and inauguration texts establish personal funds regardless. This limits above dispute rather than assigning everybody general own-funding view.
Rav Ashi distinguishes sin-offering bull plus burnt-offering ram from RH/Shavuot where both are burnt offerings.

Ravina first version compares high-priest service, excluding all objections not high-priest service. Alternate version compares initial service; question מאי תחלה rejects interpretation initially by high priest as same as first version and resolves initial service in a place. Preserve alternate-report marker and negative דלאו; no final conflation.

Rav Dimi reports Yohanan teaches one derivation (YK) and bracketed R Yehoshua b Levi two (parah and YK). Challenge from both separations answered parah is mere extra safeguard in Yohanan's own position. Challenge from earlier chain answered that was teacher's teaching: Ravin reports Yohanan in R Ishmael's name deriving both. These are distinctions in holder/report, not Yohanan retracting or contradiction unresolved.

Continuation: Resh Lakish challenges inauguration derivation's implication all matters indispensable using substitute priest wording. Yohanan asks source; Resh Lakish Sinai six-day derivation plus wife impurity extra day. Sprinkling challenge and response; two baraitot support respective derivations. 4b:12–13 explicitly identifies Yohanan as all-written indispensable by silence, distinct from Hanina; 5a discusses practical differences including separation. This is context only, not core coverage.
